AUTHORIZATION AND CONTINUITY

I authorize ongoing proof development, implementation choices, verification, saving, reviewed commits and normal pushes to this repository. Make routine decisions independently. Do not ask whether to continue, require a continuation marker, or wait for another message from me.

This automated trigger grants no additional approval for unrelated or destructive actions. Keep work within this project and its existing build environment. PROOF DEVELOPMENT

Choose the unfinished dependency that most directly advances the main theorem. Work through a meaningful bounded unit, continuing with further units when practical. Reserve time for checking and saving. Do not spend the run merely rewriting plans or progress reports.

Preserve the original theorem statements, hypotheses and exceptional cases. No sorry, unproved axioms, weakened statements or substitution of untrusted computation for the required kernel proofs. Preserve the project's existing policy on native_decide and proof verification.

Reuse accepted results when their source and dependency fingerprints still match. Avoid repeating successful builds or audits without a concrete reason. Prefer shared lemmas and existing certificate infrastructure. Split expensive finite checks into smaller kernel-checked parts and prove exact coverage. Test a representative part before generating a large batch. Integrate verified components into the dependency chain of the main theorem.

Use the existing guarded compiler commands and bounded timeouts, normally 240 seconds per costly module where supported. Collect the actual exit status and relevant output. Do not launch a duplicate because a tool returned before compilation finished. After repeated failure, change the proof or decomposition, or move to another useful obligation. Avoid identical retries and frequent polling.

SAVE AND SYNCHRONIZE

After each coherent checked unit, save its source and genuine verification evidence. Review the diff, stage only the intended files, commit and push to the existing private repository. Verify that the remote branch contains the intended commit. Include previously completed unsynchronized work when its provenance and verification are established. Do not defer commits until an entire graph family is finished.

Distinguish successful compilation, axiom/type checks, kernel replay and root integration. Describe precisely which checks passed. Keep incomplete work labeled as incomplete.

Maintain one concise current handoff with the completed unit, evidence locations, local and remote commit status, remaining obligation and next action. Before ending, settle only this run's identified child processes and release its own locks. Do not leave an unmanaged compiler or batch launcher.

CONTINUE THROUGH ORDINARY OBSTACLES

If one proof unit is blocked, work on another useful authorized unit. Diagnose ordinary build and synchronization failures independently. Preserve local work and commits if a push fails, continue useful local work, and retry transient synchronization failures on a later run.

If access is temporarily unavailable or no useful work is currently possible, report the exact obstacle briefly and leave the hourly task enabled. Reassess it on the next run without repeating the same failed operation blindly. Do not disable the task because of a timeout, failed proof attempt or missing continuation marker.

A later explicit user stop/pause instruction must be respected. Disable only this exact task after such an instruction, or after the original main theorem and required integration have been verified and synchronized. Otherwise keep the schedule enabled.

Give a short Croatian report stating what was accomplished, what was verified, the commit/push status and the next step or concrete blocker. Keep source code and project records in English. Report only work actually performed.
